# Project Overview and Environment Setup

This project investigates gut microbiome community structure and taxonomic alterations in Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) compared to non-IBD controls using public 16S rRNA sequencing data from the integrative Human Microbiome Project (iHMP / HMP2), accessed via the Bioconductor package `HMP2Data` (Stansfield et al., 2024).

The workflow integrates analytical techniques from:
- **IT4133 Bioinformatics and Computational Biology:** Community diversity, Bray-Curtis dissimilarity, UPGMA hierarchical clustering, pattern recognition, and negative binomial differential expression modeling.
- **EL4152 Machine Learning:** Supervised and unsupervised learning, $k$-means clustering, Support Vector Machines (Linear and Radial), Random Forest ensembles, rigorous data leakage prevention, cross-validation, and classification performance evaluation under the curse of dimensionality.

# Phase 0 & 1: Data Import, Inspection, and Preprocessing

## Data Loading and Initial Inspection

The primary data object is retrieved programmatically via `HMP2Data::IBD16S()`.

```{r data-import}
# Retrieve the IBD 16S phyloseq object
ps_raw <- HMP2Data::IBD16S()

cat("Raw dataset dimensions:\n")
cat("Total samples:", nsamples(ps_raw), "\n")
cat("Total taxa:", ntaxa(ps_raw), "\n")
cat("Taxonomic ranks:", paste(rank_names(ps_raw), collapse = " > "), "\n")
cat("Taxa are rows:", taxa_are_rows(ps_raw), "\n")

# Extract metadata as a standard data frame
meta_raw <- as(sample_data(ps_raw), "data.frame")
cat("Total unique participants (subject_id):", length(unique(meta_raw$subject_id)), "\n")
cat("Raw diagnosis distribution:\n")
print(table(meta_raw$diagnosis, useNA = "ifany"))
```

## Quality Control and Sample Deduplication

In clinical microbiome studies with longitudinal sampling, repeated measures from the same patient violate the assumption of independent observations required by standard statistical hypothesis tests (such as the Wilcoxon rank-sum test and PERMANOVA). To ensure statistical independence:
1. Only the earliest recorded sample per participant is retained by deterministically sorting by participant ID, visit number, and week number before deduplication.
2. Samples with sequencing depth below 1,000 reads are excluded to avoid unstable richness estimates.
3. A binary group factor is constructed (`Control` vs `IBD`, where CD and UC are merged into `IBD`).

```{r preprocessing}
# Sort deterministically by participant and longitudinal visit order
ord <- order(meta_raw$subject_id, meta_raw$visit_number, meta_raw$week_num)
meta_sorted <- meta_raw[ord, ]

# Identify the earliest sample per subject
first_samples <- rownames(meta_sorted)[!duplicated(meta_sorted$subject_id)]
ps_one <- prune_samples(first_samples, ps_raw)
cat("Samples after retaining one baseline sample per subject:", nsamples(ps_one), "\n")

# Sequencing depth filtering: retain samples with >= 1,000 reads
depths <- sample_sums(ps_one)
cat("Minimum library depth before filtering:", min(depths), "reads\n")
cat("Maximum library depth before filtering:", max(depths), "reads\n")
cat("Samples with depth < 1,000 reads:", sum(depths < 1000), "\n")

keep_samples <- names(depths)[depths >= 1000]
ps_depth <- prune_samples(keep_samples, ps_one)
cat("Samples retained after depth filtering (>= 1,000 reads):", nsamples(ps_depth), "\n")

# Construct diagnosis factors
sample_data(ps_depth)$dx3 <- factor(sample_data(ps_depth)$diagnosis, levels = c("CD", "UC", "nonIBD"))
sample_data(ps_depth)$group <- factor(
  ifelse(sample_data(ps_depth)$dx3 == "nonIBD", "Control", "IBD"),
  levels = c("Control", "IBD")
)

# Export cohort summary table
cohort_summary <- as.data.frame(table(
  Group = sample_data(ps_depth)$group,
  Diagnosis = sample_data(ps_depth)$dx3
))
write.csv(cohort_summary, file.path(fig_dir, "cohort_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

cat("Cohort breakdown after quality control:\n")
print(cohort_summary)
```

## Taxonomic Prevalence Filtering for Ecological Analyses

Low-prevalence taxa (present in fewer than 10% of samples) represent sequencing noise and inflate the penalty of multiple testing. For exploratory diversity and community clustering analyses, taxa present in at least 10% of the filtered samples are retained.

```{r prevalence-filter}
otu_mat <- as(otu_table(ps_depth), "matrix")
if (!taxa_are_rows(ps_depth)) otu_mat <- t(otu_mat)

# Calculate prevalence across samples
taxa_prev <- rowSums(otu_mat > 0)
prevalence_threshold <- 0.10 * nsamples(ps_depth)
keep_taxa_eco <- names(taxa_prev)[taxa_prev >= prevalence_threshold]

ps_filt <- prune_taxa(keep_taxa_eco, ps_depth)
cat("Taxa retained (>= 10% prevalence):", ntaxa(ps_filt), "out of", ntaxa(ps_depth), "\n")
```

---

# Phase 2: Alpha Diversity Analysis

Within-sample alpha diversity is assessed using Shannon entropy (sensitive to both richness and evenness) and the Gini-Simpson index (weighted toward dominant species). Because alpha diversity indices are sensitive to variation in sequencing depth, library sizes are rarefied to uniform sampling depth prior to metric computation (McMurdie and Holmes, 2014).

Between-group differences are tested using two-tailed Wilcoxon rank-sum tests (Mann-Whitney U), as diversity indices frequently deviate from normality.

```{r alpha-diversity}
# Rarefy to minimum observed sequencing depth
min_seq_depth <- min(sample_sums(ps_depth))
cat("Rarefying to uniform depth:", min_seq_depth, "reads\n")

ps_rarefied <- phyloseq::rarefy_even_depth(
  ps_depth,
  sample.size = min_seq_depth,
  rngseed = 42,
  verbose = FALSE
)

# Calculate alpha diversity indices
alpha_metrics <- phyloseq::estimate_richness(ps_rarefied, measures = c("Shannon", "Simpson"))
alpha_metrics$group <- sample_data(ps_rarefied)$group
alpha_metrics$sample_id <- rownames(alpha_metrics)

# Statistical hypothesis testing (Wilcoxon rank-sum test)
w_shannon <- wilcox.test(Shannon ~ group, data = alpha_metrics)
w_simpson <- wilcox.test(Simpson ~ group, data = alpha_metrics)

shannon_ctrl_med <- median(alpha_metrics$Shannon[alpha_metrics$group == "Control"])
shannon_ibd_med  <- median(alpha_metrics$Shannon[alpha_metrics$group == "IBD"])
simpson_ctrl_med <- median(alpha_metrics$Simpson[alpha_metrics$group == "Control"])
simpson_ibd_med  <- median(alpha_metrics$Simpson[alpha_metrics$group == "IBD"])

cat("Alpha Diversity Statistics:\n")
cat("Shannon Index: Control Median =", round(shannon_ctrl_med, 3),
    "; IBD Median =", round(shannon_ibd_med, 3),
    "; W =", w_shannon$statistic, "; p-value =", round(w_shannon$p.value, 4), "\n")
cat("Simpson Index: Control Median =", round(simpson_ctrl_med, 3),
    "; IBD Median =", round(simpson_ibd_med, 3),
    "; W =", w_simpson$statistic, "; p-value =", round(w_simpson$p.value, 4), "\n")

# Visualization: Alpha diversity boxplots with jitter
alpha_long <- alpha_metrics %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Shannon", "Simpson"), names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Diversity") %>%
  mutate(p_label = ifelse(Metric == "Shannon",
                          paste0("Wilcoxon p = ", round(w_shannon$p.value, 4)),
                          paste0("Wilcoxon p = ", round(w_simpson$p.value, 4))))

p_alpha <- ggplot(alpha_long, aes(x = group, y = Diversity, fill = group)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7, width = 0.5) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ Metric, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Control" = "#2b8cbe", "IBD" = "#e41a1c")) +
  geom_text(aes(x = 1.5, y = Inf, label = p_label), vjust = 1.5, check_overlap = TRUE, size = 4) +
  labs(
    title = "Alpha Diversity Comparison in Gut Microbiome (IBD vs Control)",
    subtitle = "Rarefied to uniform depth of 1,415 reads; Wilcoxon rank-sum test",
    x = "Cohort",
    y = "Diversity Metric Value"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "alpha.png"), p_alpha, width = 7, height = 5)
p_alpha
```

# Phase 3: Beta Diversity and Community Structure

Beta diversity evaluates differences in community composition across samples. Counts are transformed to relative abundance, and pairwise Bray-Curtis dissimilarities (Bray and Curtis, 1957) are computed.

Group divergence is tested via Permutational Multivariate Analysis of Variance (PERMANOVA; `vegan::adonis2`, 999 permutations). Homogeneity of multivariate dispersion is verified using `vegan::betadisper` to distinguish true community centroid shifts from within-group variance differences (Anderson, 2001; Anderson, 2006). Non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS) is employed for two-dimensional ordination.

```{r beta-diversity}
# Transform filtered counts to relative abundance
ps_rel <- phyloseq::transform_sample_counts(ps_filt, function(x) x / sum(x))

# Compute pairwise Bray-Curtis distance matrix
bc_dist <- phyloseq::distance(ps_rel, method = "bray")

# Test homogeneity of multivariate dispersion
disp_model <- vegan::betadisper(bc_dist, sample_data(ps_rel)$group)
disp_test <- anova(disp_model)
cat("Multivariate Dispersion Test (betadisper):\n")
cat("F =", round(disp_test$`F value`[1], 3), "; p-value =", round(disp_test$`Pr(>F)`[1], 4), "\n")

# PERMANOVA test
set.seed(42)
permanova_res <- vegan::adonis2(
  bc_dist ~ group,
  data = as(sample_data(ps_rel), "data.frame"),
  permutations = 999
)
cat("PERMANOVA Results (adonis2):\n")
print(permanova_res)

# NMDS Ordination
set.seed(42)
nmds_res <- phyloseq::ordinate(ps_rel, method = "NMDS", distance = "bray", trymax = 50)
cat("NMDS 2D Stress Value:", round(nmds_res$stress, 4), "\n")

# Plot NMDS ordination
nmds_points <- as.data.frame(nmds_res$points)
nmds_points$group <- sample_data(ps_rel)$group

p_nmds <- ggplot(nmds_points, aes(x = MDS1, y = MDS2, color = group, fill = group)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_ellipse(geom = "polygon", alpha = 0.2, level = 0.95, type = "t") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Control" = "#2b8cbe", "IBD" = "#e41a1c")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Control" = "#2b8cbe", "IBD" = "#e41a1c")) +
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.3,
           label = paste0("Stress = ", round(nmds_res$stress, 4),
                          "\nPERMANOVA R² = ", round(permanova_res$R2[1], 4),
                          ", p = ", permanova_res$`Pr(>F)`[1]),
           size = 4, fontface = "italic") +
  labs(
    title = "NMDS Ordination of Gut Microbial Communities (Bray-Curtis)",
    subtitle = "Points represent samples; ellipses represent 95% confidence intervals",
    x = "NMDS Axis 1",
    y = "NMDS Axis 2",
    color = "Cohort",
    fill = "Cohort"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "nmds.png"), p_nmds, width = 7, height = 5)
p_nmds
```

# Phase 4: Unsupervised Learning (IT4133 & EL4152)

Unsupervised pattern recognition explores whether unlabeled microbial abundance profiles naturally partition into clusters corresponding to clinical status.

## UPGMA Hierarchical Clustering

Unweighted Pair Group Method with Arithmetic Mean (UPGMA; Sokal and Michener, 1958) is performed using average-linkage hierarchical clustering (`hclust(..., method = "average")`) on Bray-Curtis dissimilarities. The cophenetic correlation coefficient is calculated to assess distance preservation.

```{r upgma}
# UPGMA average-linkage clustering
hc_upgma <- hclust(bc_dist, method = "average")
coph_corr <- cor(cophenetic(hc_upgma), bc_dist)
cat("UPGMA Cophenetic Correlation Coefficient:", round(coph_corr, 4), "\n")

# Convert to phylo object for tree plotting with ape
phylo_tree <- ape::as.phylo(hc_upgma)
tip_colors <- ifelse(sample_data(ps_rel)$group[match(phylo_tree$tip.label, sample_names(ps_rel))] == "Control",
                     "#2b8cbe", "#e41a1c")

png(file.path(fig_dir, "upgma_dendrogram.png"), width = 1200, height = 900, res = 150)
plot(phylo_tree, tip.color = tip_colors, cex = 0.6,
     main = paste0("UPGMA Hierarchical Clustering (Cophenetic r = ", round(coph_corr, 3), ")"))
legend("topleft", legend = c("Control", "IBD"), fill = c("#2b8cbe", "#e41a1c"), bty = "n", cex = 0.9)
dev.off()

# Display tree in notebook
plot(phylo_tree, tip.color = tip_colors, cex = 0.6,
     main = paste0("UPGMA Hierarchical Clustering (Cophenetic r = ", round(coph_corr, 3), ")"))
legend("topleft", legend = c("Control", "IBD"), fill = c("#2b8cbe", "#e41a1c"), bty = "n", cex = 0.9)

# Cut tree at k = 2
upgma_clusters <- cutree(hc_upgma, k = 2)
upgma_tab <- table(Cluster = upgma_clusters, Group = sample_data(ps_rel)$group)
ari_upgma <- mclust::adjustedRandIndex(upgma_clusters, sample_data(ps_rel)$group)

cat("UPGMA (k = 2) Cluster vs Group Contingency Table:\n")
print(upgma_tab)
cat("UPGMA Adjusted Rand Index (ARI):", round(ari_upgma, 4), "\n")
```

## $k$-Means Clustering on PCoA Coordinates

$k$-means clustering operates in Euclidean space. Non-Euclidean Bray-Curtis dissimilarities are projected into Euclidean coordinate space via Principal Coordinates Analysis (PCoA; `cmdscale`, $k = 5$). Cluster validity across $k = 2$ to $k = 6$ is evaluated using average silhouette width (`cluster::silhouette`) to identify optimal cluster separation.

```{r kmeans-clustering}
# Classical multidimensional scaling (PCoA) to Euclidean space
pcoa_coords <- cmdscale(bc_dist, k = 5)

# Silhouette analysis across k = 2 to 6
k_range <- 2:6
sil_scores <- sapply(k_range, function(k) {
  set.seed(42)
  km <- kmeans(pcoa_coords, centers = k, nstart = 25)
  ss <- cluster::silhouette(km$cluster, dist(pcoa_coords))
  mean(ss[, "sil_width"])
})

sil_df <- data.frame(k = k_range, Silhouette = sil_scores)

p_sil <- ggplot(sil_df, aes(x = k, y = Silhouette)) +
  geom_line(color = "#2c7fb8", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "#253494", size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = k_range) +
  labs(
    title = "Silhouette Analysis for k-Means Clustering on PCoA Coordinates",
    subtitle = "Evaluated on first 5 PCoA axes of Bray-Curtis dissimilarities",
    x = "Number of Clusters (k)",
    y = "Average Silhouette Width"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "kmeans_silhouette.png"), p_sil, width = 7, height = 4.5)
p_sil

# Fit k-means with k = 2
set.seed(42)
km_res <- kmeans(pcoa_coords, centers = 2, nstart = 25)
km_tab <- table(Cluster = km_res$cluster, Group = sample_data(ps_rel)$group)
ari_kmeans <- mclust::adjustedRandIndex(km_res$cluster, sample_data(ps_rel)$group)

cat("k-means (k = 2) Cluster vs Group Contingency Table:\n")
print(km_tab)
cat("k-means Adjusted Rand Index (ARI):", round(ari_kmeans, 4), "\n")
```

### Interpretation Guard
The low Adjusted Rand Index values observed in both UPGMA ($\text{ARI} = -0.0154$) and $k$-means ($\text{ARI} = -0.0112$) indicate that unsupervised clustering does not automatically recover the binary disease phenotype. This does not indicate that the microbiota lacks clinical relevance; rather, unsupervised methods capture dominant ecological gradients (such as enterotype variations, mucosal moisture, or dominant commensal community states) that can cut across clinical labels.
